title: Deployment risk acceptance workbook — RBAC v2 + SIEM mapping
content:
Purpose:
This workbook is a lightweight, deployable artifact to support release decisioning when RBAC v2, audit logging schema changes, or SIEM export mapping are in scope. It centralizes the risk matrix, required evidence artifacts, auto-collection hooks, and an approval surface for exceptions and conditional launch decisions.

Scope & When to use: 
- Use this when any of the following are true for a release / rollout: RBAC role changes (v2 migration or additions), audit log schema updates, or changes to SIEM export/field mappings.
- Not for purely app-level feature changes with no auth or logging surface impact.

Owner & reviewers: 
- Primary owner: Jordan Nguyen (security) — responsible for compiling evidence and driving sign-offs.
- Reviewers: eng infra, SRE, compliance, product PM for the release.

1) Quick risk snapshot (one-line)
- Change: RBAC v2 role "service-deployer" added + audit event "deployer.grant" + SIEM mapping change for field "actor_id" -> "user.id"
- Risk summary: Moderate — introduces a new deploy-capable role and changes event schema used by alerting. Requires evidence that role scoping is correct and SIEM rules/refactors updated.

2) Risk matrix (use for go/no-go)
- Severity: Critical / High / Medium / Low
- Likelihood: Frequent / Possible / Unlikely

Matrix (examples):
- Critical x Frequent = BLOCK unless compensating controls (automated attestation + canary rollback) in place.
- High x Possible = Requires conditional approval and 24h post-launch monitoring plan.
- Medium x Possible = Requires QA and evidence captured; can proceed after reviewer approval.
- Low x Unlikely = Proceed with standard release guardrails.

3) Acceptance criteria checklist (all items must be answered yes or have an exception approved)
- RBAC correctness: role definitions reviewed and documented (yes/no). Link to role matrix.
- Least privilege: evidence that new role does not include extraneous privileges (yes/no).
- Role assignment flow: scripted role provisioning exists and has integration tests (yes/no).
- Audit logging: all auth and grant events emitted using canonical audit schema (yes/no).
- SIEM mapping: downstream SIEM parsing rules updated and test alerts executed (yes/no).
- Backout plan: rollback steps defined and tested in staging (yes/no).
- Canary: rollout plan includes staged rollout and circuit breaker (yes/no).
- Monitoring: dashboards and alert thresholds created for 48–72h monitoring window (yes/no).
- Evidence automation: automated evidence collector run succeeded (yes/no).

4) Required evidence artifacts (attach links or automation outputs)
- RBAC role matrix (CSV/Google sheet) showing new role -> permissions mapping.
- Automated unit/integration test run showing role gating enforced (CI job link).
- Audit log sample: example events (raw JSON) demonstrating new fields and schema.
- SIEM parsing test output: show extracted fields, normalized actor id, and sample alert firing in test environment.
- Playbook: rollback steps and expected duration to reduce blast radius.
- Canaries: traffic-shift plan and success criteria.
- Threat model update: short note capturing new attack surface if applicable.

5) Audit log schema mapping (canonical fields we require)
- canonical_event_id: unique id for the event (UUID).
- timestamp: ISO-8601 UTC event time.
- service: logical service name (e.g. "redwood-deployer").
- event_type: logical event name (e.g. "deployer.grant").
- actor.type: user | service | api-key.
- actor.id: stable identifier (prefer human id or service id).
- target.type: resource type (e.g. "deployment", "model").
- target.id: resource identifier.
- outcome: success | failure | partial.
- metadata: freeform JSON string with contextual attrs.

Notes: fields must be present for events that affect auth and deployment. Avoid changing field names without a SIEM mapping entry and test evidence.

6) SIEM export mapping & common gotchas
- Mapping guidance: map canonical names to SIEM columns (example below). Keep a one-line rationale for any transform.

Example mapping lines (to paste into SIEM mapping ticket):
- canonical_event_id -> siem.event_id (string)
- timestamp -> siem.timestamp (epoch_ms -> ISO conversion note)
- service -> siem.source.service
- event_type -> siem.event.action
- actor.type -> siem.actor.type
- actor.id -> siem.actor.id
- target.type -> siem.target.type
- target.id -> siem.target.id
- outcome -> siem.event.outcome
- metadata -> siem.event.metadata (json-string)

Common gotchas:
- Field renames break saved SIEM queries/alert rules. Include mapping for each renamed field.
- Null or empty actor.id can cause alerts to drop; ensure fallback mapping or a non-null surrogate.
- Timezone/epoch conversions: confirm consistent epoch -> iso conversions and rounding.
- Nested JSON in metadata may not be indexed by SIEM — explicit flattening may be required.

7) Evidence automation hooks (how to produce artifacts)
- evidence-collector job (CI): repo: infra/tools/evidence-collector — runs after staging deploy, collects: sample audit logs (tail 5m), role inventory snapshot, SIEM parse test, and stores artifacts in GCS under gs://redwood-audit-evidence/<release-id>.
- smoke-siem-runner: small test harness that sends synthetic events to SIEM ingest and validates parsing rules. Output: pass/fail + sample parsed JSON. Use ticket tag SEC-<release-id>.
- RBAC linter: infra/scripts/rbac-lint.sh — validates role docs against schema and flags wildcard permissions.

8) SIEM validation queries (examples to run in test index)
- find events where event_type == "deployer.grant" and actor.type == "service" and outcome == "success"; verify actor.id normalized.
- alert smoke: run alert rule in test index to ensure it triggers for a synthetic failed grant event.

9) Exception handling and temporary mitigations (if a checklist item fails)
- Short-term mitigations must be documented and timeboxed (max 72h) and approved by Head of Security.
- Exceptions require: mitigation description, compensating control evidence, owner, and expiry date.
- Example mitigations: restricted IP allowlist, reduced blast radius via feature-flag gating, elevated monitoring (1m alerting).

10) Approval template (capture final decisions)
- Release id: _______________________
- Release lead: _______________________
- Risk rating (from matrix): _______________________
- Conditional launch? (yes/no) If yes, list conditions: _______________________
- Exception required? (yes/no). If yes, exception link: _______________________

Signatures:
- Security reviewer: name, role, date, note
- Eng infra reviewer: name, role, date, note
- Product owner: name, role, date, note
- Compliance (if required): name, role, date, note

11) Post-launch verification checklist (first 72 hours)
- Continuous audit log export check every 15m for presence of new event types.
- SIEM parsing health: run smoke-siem-runner hourly for first 6 hours, then every 4 hours.
- Canary metrics: error rate, latency, unauthorized access attempts.
- Rollback on predefined thresholds (documented in playbook).

12) Sample short-form notes (notes-to-self / meeting fragment style)
- "Maya to update SIEM mapping PR by EOD Thurs — need to include epoch->iso conversion example. Also add a non-null actor.id mapping."
- "Owen to run evidence-collector after staging deploy and upload to GCS; link should be added to this workbook."
- "If RBAC linter flags wildcard:* permission, require manual pair-review before merge."

Appendix A: quick checklist (one-line):
- [ ] Role docs in sheet + reviewer signoff
- [ ] RBAC linter passed or exception documented
- [ ] Audit log samples present (raw JSON)
- [ ] SIEM parse tests passed
- [ ] Canary & rollback plan in place
- [ ] Evidence artifacts uploaded to GCS + linked below

Appendix B: artifact links (populate during review)
- Evidence bucket: gs://redwood-audit-evidence/<release-id>
- RBAC sheet: [link placeholder]
- CI run (evidence-collector): [link placeholder]
- SIEM mapping PR: [link placeholder]

-- end workbook --

Revision notes: created initial draft 2024-11-02. Updated SIEM mapping examples and added evidence automation hooks 2024-11-18.
